readme: Bevel Tactile, skeuomorphic React components for real product work. Built on Base UI and Tailwind CSS v4, installed with the shadcn CLI. bevel-ui.vercel.app: docs, every component, and live demos. Each component is a physical object that does a real job in a modern app: a cover over a deploy switch, alarm lamps that latch until someone sees them, a fader an agent can move and you can take back, a library slip for an expiring API key. Like shadcn/ui, it isn't a package: the source lands in your project and it's yours. Install Add the registry to components.json once: { "registries": { "@bevel": "https://bevel-ui.vercel.app/r/{name}.json" } } Then add components by name: npx shadcn@latest add @bevel/guarded-switch @bevel/annunciator Or skip the setup and install straight from a URL: npx shadcn@latest add https://bevel-ui.vercel.app/r/wallet.json Every demo product also installs as a whole screen (a block) in a Next.js app: npx shadcn@latest add @bevel/agent-console # or billing-desk, release-hall, review-desk You need React 19, Tailwind CSS v4 and a project set up with npx shadcn@latest init. See the installation guide. What's inside Category Components Money Wallet, Payment card, Amount, Meter, Receipt, Ticket sheet, Ledger, Keycard Instruments Number wheel, Gauge and dial, Breaker, Engine telegraph, Annunciator, Detent knob, Push to talk, Motorized fader, Mixer strip Coordination Guarded switch, Dead man's switch, Lockout, Take a number Records Keysort filter, Visible file, Contact sheet, Split-flap board, Due-date slip Agents Name tag, Task plan, Activity log, Approval, Delegation board Documents Citation, Redline Marks Stamp and seal, Redaction Demos Four made-up products, each one screen built from Bevel components. Every demo also installs as a whole screen, e.g. npx shadcn@latest add @bevel/agent-console. Principles A real job first. If a plain control does the job as well, it isn't in Bevel. Composable parts, never mega-props. A part that works alone is its own component. Tokens, not values. Components read one foundation stylesheet; a lint fails on raw colours, durations or lengths. One light, from above, so every highlight and shadow agrees. State in words. What an object shows with light or position, it also says in text. Compositor-only motion. Transform, opacity and filter; never layout. Read more in the design system and accessibility guides. Repository packages/ui the components and their stylesheets (what ships) apps/web docs site; also serves the registry at /r/{name}.json apps/storybook stories, run as browser tests with axe checks scripts registry build and the token lint pnpm install pnpm dev # docs site on :3000 pnpm storybook # Storybook on :6006 pnpm --filter storybook test # every story as a browser test pnpm check:tokens # design-system lint Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Please read CONTRIBUTING.md first. New components especially need a clear job that no existing component already does. Author Made by @_hiteshbandhu on X.
